sentiment.instructions: Judge the feeling the tweet's author clearly expresses (about events, people, plans, products), not merely the topic. Pick positive or negative only when the emotion is strong and explicit; otherwise choose neutral.

criteria.positive: Clear, explicit enthusiasm, praise, love, gratitude or celebration: 'can't wait', 'so excited', 'love', 'best', 'amazing', 'congrats', 'good luck', strong fandom praise. Also sympathy and support: prayers, condolences, 'RIP', 'God bless'. Reports of victories, titles or achievements framed approvingly count too. Merely mentioning a plan or event, or a lone ':)' or '<3', is not enough.
criteria.neutral: Facts, headlines, scores, schedules, play-by-play, ads, spam and info sessions. Plans or intentions stated without strong emotion ('going to the game Friday', 'X is the move tomorrow', 'gonna watch...'). Requests to celebrities, plain or rhetorical questions, trivia, jokes and banter. Mild self-deprecating grumbling ('lmao', 'I'm dead', 'why did I...', a busy day tomorrow). Reported criticism or speculation without the author's own strong feeling. Mixed or mild opinions. When the cues are weak or ambiguous, choose neutral.
criteria.negative: Explicit strong anger, disappointment, sadness, contempt or hostility from the author: 'WTF', 'FML', 'sucks', 'hate', 'worst', 'pissed', 'disappointed', insults, profanity at someone, bitter sarcasm, political or religious attacks. Also reports focused on clearly harmful events such as attacks, missiles, deaths, crashes and economic losses.
